name: Muse Three.js 1: harden the pilot pipeline
description: Puts tests around the pilot scripts (briefs, teacher generation, validator, dataset builder), fixes the lopsided domain sampling seen in the 51-brief pilot, makes the validator reusable and resumable, and adds a pilot report with a screenshot contact sheet. No new pipeline stages yet.

userStories.title: Test harness and build_dataset tests
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want a test harness and tests for the dataset builder so that changes to how training data is joined and split cannot silently corrupt it.
steps: Add requirements-dev.txt with pytest and install it into .venv (`.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-dev.txt`).
Create tests/py/conftest.py that puts scripts/ on sys.path, and tests/fixtures/ with a tiny set of briefs, raw answers and a validation report (6 briefs across 3 levels, 2 failing, 1 with reasoning).
Refactor scripts/build_dataset.py so the work is done by `build(briefs, raw_dir, report, out_dir, no_reasoning, val_fraction, seed)` returning counts; main() only parses args and calls it.

Write tests/py/test_build_dataset.py: only ok rows are kept; reasoning is wrapped in <think> tags unless no_reasoning; the split is stratified by level and deterministic for a seed; prompt/completion roles are system,user / assistant.
acceptanceCriteria: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/py` runs and passes with at least 4 tests for build_dataset
build_dataset.build is importable without side effects and main() output for the fixtures is unchanged from before the refactor (same kept count and same train/val ids)
requirements-dev.txt exists and README quickstart mentions how to run the tests
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: teacher_generate: pure parsing and retry tests
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want the answer parsing and retry rules tested so that reasoning traces and failed calls are handled the same way for every backend.
steps: Extract pure functions from scripts/teacher_generate.py: `split_reasoning(content, reasoning_field)` (separate field, inline <think>...</think>, or none) and `is_retryable(status)` (429 and 5xx retry, other 4xx do not).
Make `call()` use them. Keep behaviour identical for the OpenAI route and the --ollama-native route.

Write tests/py/test_teacher_generate.py with a fake client object: reasoning field wins, inline think is split and stripped, no reasoning gives None, a 404 is not retried, a 429 is retried then succeeds (patch time.sleep), finish_reason 'length' is recorded.
Add a test that main() skips briefs whose raw file already exists and does not save failed calls (drive it with a fake client via monkeypatch).
Keep the `--token-budget` flag (added after the Spark Open runs) and test it: with a budget of 1 token the second brief is skipped and reported as skipped, and in-flight calls still save.
acceptanceCriteria: split_reasoning and is_retryable exist and are covered by at least 6 tests
A rerun with all raw files present makes zero model calls (asserted in a test)
No test touches the network or sleeps for real (time.sleep is patched)
A test shows `--token-budget` stops starting new calls once the budget is used and the summary line reports skipped briefs
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: gen_briefs: balanced domains and parsing tests
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want briefs spread evenly across domains and levels so that the student is not trained mostly on nature scenes (the 51-brief pilot had 16 nature briefs and no sci-fi, historical, data-viz or voxel ones).
steps: Replace the shuffled itertools.cycle in scripts/gen_briefs.py with a balanced schedule: round-robin over domains, and within each domain rotate level and style, so after N briefs every domain has N/12 within plus or minus 1. Keep --seed deterministic.
Extract `parse_brief_lines(text, domain, level, style)` as a pure function; it must accept lines wrapped in code fences, trailing commas and a leading list marker, and ignore prose lines.

Write tests/py/test_gen_briefs.py: near_dup catches reordered words and ignores unrelated briefs; parse_brief_lines cases; the schedule for 120 briefs gives each of the 12 domains exactly 10 and covers levels 1 to 10 in every domain; the empty-answer abort fires after 10 empty answers (fake client).
acceptanceCriteria: For a schedule of 120 briefs every one of the 12 domains appears exactly 10 times (asserted in a test)
parse_brief_lines accepts fenced and comma-terminated JSON lines and skips malformed ones
gen_briefs.py still writes data/briefs.jsonl and data/briefs.eval.jsonl with the same field names (id, title, brief, domain, level, style)
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: Validator as a testable module
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want the validator's checks in an importable module with tests so that threshold tuning is safe.
steps: Move extractHtml, staticChecks, the pixel statistics and the frame diff from scripts/validate_scenes.mjs into scripts/lib/validate.mjs as named exports; validate_scenes.mjs imports them and behaves exactly as before.
Make thresholds (BLANK_MIN_COLORS, STATIC_MIN_DIFF, WAIT_MS) exports of the module so tests and the CLI share them.

Write tests/js/validate.unit.test.mjs with node:test: extractHtml (fenced, bare doctype, none); staticChecks (examples/jsm import, OrbitControls, a second external import, a script src, eval, missing animation loop, a clean scene); pixel stats and diff on PNGs built in the test with pngjs (flat colour, two-colour, identical frames, shifted frames).
Check that `node scripts/validate_scenes.mjs --raw tests/fixtures/raw --scenes <tmp> --shots <tmp> --report <tmp>/r.jsonl` still runs on the fixture raw files from US-001.

Cover import maps in staticChecks tests: a bare `three` mapped to the pinned CDN URL passes (Spark Open writes scenes this way), a map to any other URL is external_dep, and invalid import-map JSON is bad_importmap.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/lib/validate.mjs exports extractHtml, staticChecks and the pixel helpers; `npm test` runs at least 10 unit tests and passes
validate_scenes.mjs imports from the module and no logic is duplicated between the two files
The unit tests need no browser
The import-map cases (pinned CDN passes, other URL fails, bad JSON fails) are tested
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

userStories.title: Validator: resume, filters, summary and real-browser tests
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want to revalidate only what changed and trust the validator against real pages so that a thousand-scene run can be resumed and tuned.
steps: Tune the static check: the Glimmer pilot rejected scenes with gentle motion (frame diff 0.0006 to 0.0018, e.g. a swaying lamp). Take 4 screenshots 500 ms apart instead of 2 and use the largest diff; keep a scene whose largest diff is at least STATIC_MIN_DIFF. Record before/after counts on the fixture scenes in notes (do not touch data/).

Add flags to scripts/validate_scenes.mjs: `--skip-done` (keep rows already in the report whose raw file is unchanged by mtime, validate only the rest), `--only id1,id2`, and `--concurrency N` (default 4).
Write `<report>.summary.json` next to the report: total, passed, pass rate, counts per reason, and counts per level and domain when the raw file carries them in `brief`.

Add tests/js/validate.e2e.test.mjs that writes small raw answers into a temp dir and runs the validator CLI: a rotating cube (ok), an empty scene with a background only (blank), a scene that throws at load (js_error), a scene with no animation (static), a truncated answer (truncated). Skip with a clear message if Chromium cannot launch.
Add a test that `--skip-done` on a finished run revalidates zero scenes.
acceptanceCriteria: The e2e test asserts the exact reason set for each of the 5 fixture scenes
`--skip-done` revalidates nothing when every raw file is unchanged (asserted)
The summary file has total, passed, passRate and a reasons map and is valid JSON
docs/03-pipeline-walkthrough.md lists the new flags
A fixture scene with a slow sway (a small object rotating 0.2 rad per second) passes and a truly still scene is still static (asserted)
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names
Browser-driven tests run against the installed Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` is already done); if Chromium cannot launch, say so in `notes` instead of skipping silently

userStories.title: Pilot report and contact sheet
userStories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want one command that turns a validated run into numbers and a screenshot grid so that I can judge a batch in a minute.
steps: Create scripts/pilot_report.py: reads data/raw, data/validation.jsonl and data/shots (paths overridable) and writes data/pilot-report.md and data/contact-sheet.html.

The report lists: kept and total, pass rate overall and by level and domain, failure reasons, median and p90 output tokens and seconds per scene (from raw usage; 'not measured' when absent), total generation time, and a projection of hours for 1,000 and 6,000 scenes at the measured median.
The contact sheet is one self-contained HTML file: a grid of screenshots (relative paths) each captioned with id, title, level and pass or fail reasons; failed ones have a red border.

Write tests/py/test_pilot_report.py with the fixtures from US-001: assert the markdown contains the pass rate, the reason counts and 'not measured' when usage is missing, and the HTML references every shot.
acceptanceCriteria: `python scripts/pilot_report.py --help` documents every path flag and the report is deterministic for the same input
Projections are computed from measured medians only and say 'not measured' otherwise (asserted)
README.md pipeline section links the report as the step after validation
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names

readFirst: README.md (pipeline table) and docs/03-pipeline-walkthrough.md (each stage's contract)
scripts/gen_briefs.py, scripts/teacher_generate.py, scripts/validate_scenes.mjs, scripts/build_dataset.py (the code under test)
metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is verified with unit tests, mocked HTTP and, for the validator, local headless Chromium. Nothing calls Ollama or any remote model.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.

The completion tag is matched literally by the harness. Write it only when every acceptance criterion holds. When a criterion cannot hold yet, never type the tag, not even inside a sentence saying you are not using it; write 'no completion signal this iteration' instead.

chromium: Browser-driven tests run against the installed Chromium (`npx playwright install chromium` is already done); if Chromium cannot launch, say so in `notes` instead of skipping silently
